svg.title: ssmcp setup and login: SSH first, OAuth next
svg.desc: First register the public key in the server account's authorized_keys. Start ssmcp in the local project and keep it running. Add the returned MCP URL to an OAuth-capable MCP client, then enter the one-time login_code on its authorization page. The MCP client uses an access token to call list and code_mode and can renew it using a rotating refresh token. A login code expires 30 minutes after issue and can be used once. Disconnecting the SSH connection that issued it revokes that connection's OAuth grants.
svg.text: Your key connects the machine. A one-time code authorizes the MCP client.
Server: ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. The private key stays local.
SSH verifies the key. The terminal prints url and login_code.
Add the URL to your MCP client
OAuth opens a login page. Paste the code once; PKCE completes login.
Discover clients. Call their local tools.
MCP uses renewable tokens. Keep the source SSH connection running.
Source SSH disconnects → its grant is revoked.
